CaseDetailPresenterDTO.description:
Presents one case card: the case, its complaints and its verdicts.

The target's live CONTENT is not here — it is fetched by the view through
``content_function`` and attached as its own envelope, because a read that
can fail must be able to say so without failing the whole card.

CaseEventPresenterDTO.description: Presents one audit row. Read-only everywhere, by declaration.

CasePresenterDTO.description: Presents one row of the cross-target moderator queue.

subject_user_id.description: Author of the moderated content, learned from content_function.

claimed_until.description: Lease expiry; past it the case returns to the queue.

PolicyDisclosureDTO.description: DSA Art. 15(1)(e) — what this deployment actually does, from the code.

ReportCreate.description:
A complaint (DSA Art. 16(2)).

``good_faith`` is the Art. 16(2)(d) declaration and defaults to False:
a checkbox nobody ticked is a checkbox nobody ticked. Whether
``description`` is required depends on the reason's
``requires_description``, which is a registry question and is therefore
answered in the service, not here — and, unlike legacy, an unwanted
description is never silently erased.

ReportPresenterDTO.description: Presents one complaint to a moderator.

reporter_id.description: Null once the reporter's account was erased.

evidence.description: The reporter's own snapshot of a target nobody serves (evidence-based target types). Unverified by construction: render it as what the complainant says they saw.

ReportResultDTO.description:
The whole answer to an accepted complaint.

Carries ``case_ref`` (a short prefix) rather than the case id: the
reporter needs something to quote at support, not a handle to a resource
they may not read.

SanctionCreate.description:
A sanction issued on its own, outside a verdict.

``case_id`` is optional in the request and mandatory in the model: when
it is absent the service opens a ``manual`` case so the sanction still
has exactly one audit trail behind it.

SanctionRequest.description: The optional sanction attached to a verdict.

StatsDTO.description: Queue counters for the console header and DSA Art. 24(1) reporting.

VerdictRequest.description:
A moderator's decision, optionally with the consequence in one act.

"Take it down AND suspend the seller AND tell them why" is one button in
the console and one transaction here; legacy needed three screens and
recorded two of them nowhere.
